RESULT. Among the (k,x) rational cycles, let S be the set of least members; the CIRCUIT holds the least element of S and the HIGH CYCLE the greatest. Steiner 1977 excludes integer circuits, whose word is 1^x 0^(k-x) with f = (3^x - 2^x)/(2^k - 3^x), using Baker-derived lower bounds on 2^k - 3^x (Ellison). Knight excludes integer HIGH cycles with NO deep bounds. The high-cycle word is the upper Christoffel word v_h with 1s at d_i = floor(k i / x). By Cohn 1972 its reverse is a rotation of it, so f(v_h) and f(v_h^R) lie in one cycle; by Berstel et al, for aperiodic v_h, v_h = 1 u 0 and v_h^R = 0 u 1, whence f(v_h) = (2g(u) + 3^(x-1))/(2^k - 3^x) and f(v_h^R) = (6g(u) + 2^(k-1))/(2^k - 3^x). If both were integers so would be 3 f(v_h) - f(v_h^R) + 1 = 2^(k-1)/(2^k - 3^x), impossible since the gap is odd. IDENTIFICATIONS WITH THIS LABORATORY, verified numerically.
